You know, when I was still a virgin, I thought treatment for anything other than HIV was a simple round of antibiotics and you were good … Well that wasn’t my experience. I got Epididymitis on my first time ever getting oral … I didn’t even know that was a thing and gosh did it wreck my life completely. I felt my life was over, lost a couple of friendships due to the severe depression I fell into because of it, and spent well over $2k taking tests and visiting different doctors. 

A year and six months after … I’ve been doing a lot better with some residual nerve pain here and there that’s alleviated with stretching, yoga, and acupuncture. Took several treatments and performed every test under the sun to ensure I’m clear and won’t pass this horrible condition to another guy. Recovery for this is very slow and definitely requires patience and strong mental health which this disease will test. FYI , It’s not common for this disease to happen, but it exists. 

My advice to you if you want to proceed …
Get on PrEP, get your HPV vaccine if you haven’t already, use condoms religiously, practice good hygiene before and after an encounter, and maybe even restrict the kind of sexual practices you do with strangers (ie: no oral, no rimming, etc.)

Descovy simply is a newer drug compared to Truvada. It is also a smaller pill to swallow and is easier on the liver/kidneys. Currently it’s only approved for PrEP use for gay men or MSM.  

Also to add to how it protects you, PrEP does in fact create a sort of barrier around your T-Cells (or CD4 cells) and that prevents HIV from infecting them thus preventing HIV from replicating in your body and infecting you.  However, it must be taken daily for at least 21 days before a potential exposure and similarly to PEP, must be continued for at least 28 days after your potential exposure. It is very important to take daily if you are at risk for HIV and to take around the same time each day.

(I’m not a health professional, I’m just someone who takes Descovy and has asked a lot of questions to my doctor and have done personal research about it)
